facts.fact: The Ministry of Local Government's annual report for financial year 2023-2024 says its Digital Office works in real time with the twelve digital offices of the local authorities through the Council Project Management system, a shared platform on which employees at every level do their daily tasks, projects and jobs are tracked in real time and staff can work remotely; the report does not say how the council offices are connected.

The Ministry's annual report says the local authorities processed 24,393 applications for Building and Land Use Permits between 1 July 2023 and 30 June 2024 in the National Electronic Licensing System, the online system the Ministry's Land Use and Planning Unit manages.

The Ministry's annual report for 2023-2024 says the I-Council system, piloted at the District Council of Moka from 27 August 2018 and extended by Government decision of 16 March 2020, was implemented in all local authorities over three years, and that the Ministry works in real time with the twelve digital offices of the local authorities, which it counts as five municipal councils and seven district councils (12 of 12); the share is of authorities working in the shared system, and no connection is described.

The Ministry's annual report for 2023-2024 says the Council Project Management system was built in-house by a team of the District Council of Moka, extended to the other local authorities by Government decision of 16 March 2020, and is run from a Digital Office at the Ministry of Local Government and Disaster Risk Management.

note: Read whole. The facts rest on the working-online rule: the report describes councils working in real time in shared systems and never describes a connection, so no `connected` fact is written. The 100 per cent is the Ministry's 'all LAs' beside its own count of twelve, and is a share working in the system, which the parent may prefer to read as computerised.
